h1:
Samut Songkhram (Mae Klong) Food
12 Things You Have to Try
intro: Samut Songkhram is Thailand's smallest province, but its appetite is anything but small. Sitting where the Mae Klong River meets the Gulf of Thailand, it gets fresh seafood at almost every meal — from the famous razor clams of Don Hoi Lot and the real bent-neck mackerel to fat river prawns, plus everything you can eat along the Amphawa floating market in the evening and the canalside cafes that keep popping up. Here are 12 things locals in Mae Klong actually eat and you shouldn't skip.

blocks.html: Just over an hour from Bangkok, Samut Songkhram is the kind of weekend food trip people keep coming back to. The charm is that the eating is spread across distinct areas: the town of Mae Klong is all about mackerel and morning markets, Don Hoi Lot is a strip of seaside seafood shops, Amphawa is an evening floating market plus canalside cafes, and Khlong Khone is mangrove-edge seafood. Plan the order well and you can eat all day without repeating yourself.

If you're coming all the way to Samut Songkhram, seafood is the main reason — especially the razor clams the province is known for. You'll find them fresh around Don Hoi Lot at the mouth of the Mae Klong River, and the egg-bearing crabs, river prawns and grouper are fresh too because they're brought in day by day.

items.name: Stir-fried razor clams (pad cha or with chili paste)
items.blurb: The province's star dish. Razor clams are long, tube-shaped clams dug from the mudflats at Don Hoi Lot at low tide — the meat is sweet and bouncy. Stir-fried pad cha with chili and holy basil, or with roasted chili paste and sweet basil, eaten piping hot — that's the high point of the meal.
items.meta: Don Hoi Lot · from THB 120–200 a plate

items.name: Grilled river prawns
items.blurb: Big river prawns, rich and full of roe, grilled over fire and dipped in tangy seafood sauce. They're a favorite both at the riverside shops along the Mae Klong and at the Amphawa floating market in the evening. Order by the piece; the price moves with the size.

items.name: Steamed egg crab / crab in curry powder
items.blurb: Sea crabs from the river mouth — firm and packed with roe. Steamed, the meat tastes naturally sweet; or stir-fried in curry powder with a rich egg sauce. You'll find it at the seafood shops around Don Hoi Lot and Khlong Khone.
items.meta: Don Hoi Lot / Khlong Khone · market price

items.name: Blanched cockles / baked scallops with butter
items.blurb: A side to go with your seafood. Cockles blanched just to that point where they're still juicy and a little bloody, dipped in seafood sauce; scallops baked with butter and garlic are a strong seller at the Amphawa floating market.
items.meta: Amphawa / Don Hoi Lot · from THB 80–150

items.name: Grilled squid / squid with salted egg
items.blurb: Fresh squid grilled until fragrant, dipped in spicy jaew sauce — easy to eat as you walk the floating market. Squid stir-fried with salted egg is a rice-side dish the seafood shops do well.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Fresh razor clams are at their best around low tide at Don Hoi Lot. Check the tide table before you go — show up at high tide and all you'll see is open sea, with no chance to watch the diggers at work.

blocks.text: Mae Klong mackerel — worth eating at the source

blocks.html: Mention Mae Klong and you have to think of bent-neck mackerel. It stands out because the mackerel from the Mae Klong bay are plump, with firm, rich meat — fishermen steam them and arrange them in small woven baskets, and because the baskets are tight, the necks get bent to make them fit. That distinctive look is how you know it's from Mae Klong at a glance.

items: Steamed mackerel in a basket — fried up crisp and eaten with shrimp-paste chili dip and fresh vegetables. It's the lunchtime spread that every household in Mae Klong eats.
Salt-braised mackerel / sour mackerel soup — braised sweet-salty until the flavor soaks in, or in a light, mildly sour clear soup. Simple home-style dishes the local shops cook well.

Mackerel to take home — shops in the Mae Klong market like Da Mae Klong Mackerel (Da Pla Thu Mae Klong) steam their own every day, and you can buy a basket to take home. Tell them you've got a long trip ahead so they pack it well.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Real Mae Klong mackerel costs a little more than ordinary mackerel, because the genuine catch is limited to the fishing season. If you spot it selling unusually cheap, ask where it's from first — some vendors steam mackerel brought in from elsewhere and sell it as the local kind.

The Amphawa floating market runs from late afternoon into the evening, only on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and long weekends. The draw is eating along the canal while you watch vendors paddle their boats — there's savory food, sweets and seafood grilled right off the boats.

items.name: Grilled seafood off the boats
items.blurb: Grilled prawns, grilled squid and scallops baked with butter, cooked fresh on boats along the canal. Order, then sit down and eat right by the water.

items.name: Canalside noodles & pad thai
items.blurb: Small stalls along the walkway do noodle soup, pad thai and oyster omelets at friendly prices — something to line your stomach before you keep walking.

items.name: Old-style Thai sweets
items.blurb: Thong yip, thong yot, khanom krok and other warm Thai sweets, plus chilled young-coconut jelly — the classic desserts of Amphawa.

items.name: Coconut water & herbal drinks
items.blurb: Amphawa is coconut country, so fresh coconut water and cold herbal drinks help beat the heat while you walk the market.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: For the full market buzz, come on a Saturday evening — but if you'd rather avoid the crowds, try Friday or Sunday evening when it's quieter, then carry on with a firefly boat tour after dark.

blocks.text: Cafes along the canal and the Mae Klong

blocks.html: Lately Amphawa has seen a lot of new cafes open, many of them set along the canal or in the middle of a coconut grove — good for an afternoon break before the market gets going. Most do coffee, sweets and one-plate meals.

items.name: Sriphala Amphawa
items.blurb: A terracotta-toned cafe in a coconut grove, with a pond and a small canal ringing the place — a mellow setting, with seating both indoors and out. The menu covers coffee, bakery and food, and the standout is the young-coconut cream puff.
items.meta: Soi Ban Khlong Khaek, Amphawa · drinks from THB 70–120

items.name: The Pomelo Amphawa (Krua Som-O Wan)
items.blurb: Part cafe, part riverside restaurant near the Amphawa market, mixing Thai food with natural views. There's fresh seafood and house-recipe desserts — good for a proper meal followed by coffee.
items.meta: Near Amphawa floating market · food from THB 120–300

items.name: 83 Coff
items.blurb: A cafe on the canal by the Amphawa market with plenty of photo corners. The signature is its chewy soft cookies — a good spot to sip a coffee before walking the market in the evening.
items.meta: Canalside, Amphawa market · drinks from THB 60–110

items.name: Pava Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A riverside cafe and restaurant in a modern-Thai style, serving coffee and homemade sweets with a river view — good for settling in for a long afternoon.

blocks.text: Mae Klong morning market and takeaway gifts

blocks.html: The town of Mae Klong has a fresh market that's busy from early morning, including the Maeklong Railway Market (Talat Rom Hup) — the market on the train tracks where vendors pull their awnings back as the train passes, then re-open them after. It's both a sight to see and a place to buy fresh food.

items: Maeklong Railway Market (the market on the tracks) — vegetables, fruit, fresh seafood and mackerel. Time your walk around the train's scheduled arrivals.
Coconut sweets — real coconut sugar, khanom tan (palm cake) and coconut-milk jelly: local desserts made from the coconuts of Amphawa's groves.
Pomelo & Mae Klong khom lychee — famous seasonal fruit. Khom lychee is sweet and fragrant and pomelo has firm flesh — both make good gifts during the fruit season.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Only a few trains run through the Maeklong Railway Market each day. If you want to catch the awning-folding moment, check the arrival and departure times at Mae Klong station first, then go stand at a safe spot to wait.

faq.q: What food should I try in Samut Songkhram?
faq.a: First, the razor clams at Don Hoi Lot, stir-fried pad cha or with roasted chili paste. After that, the bent-neck Mae Klong mackerel, grilled river prawns, steamed egg crab, and the eats along the Amphawa floating market in the evening — finishing with Thai sweets and coconut desserts.

faq.q: When can I eat fresh razor clams at Don Hoi Lot?
faq.a: You'll see people digging razor clams and find the most fresh ones around low tide, so check the tide table before you go — at high tide you'll only see the sea. The restaurants along Don Hoi Lot serve razor-clam dishes most of the day, though.

faq.q: What days is the Amphawa floating market open, and what food is there?
faq.a: The Amphawa floating market is open only on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings and long weekends, from late afternoon into the evening. There's seafood grilled off the boats, grilled prawns and squid, noodles, pad thai, old-style Thai sweets, and fresh coconut water.

faq.q: What is bent-neck Mae Klong mackerel, and where do I buy it to take home?
faq.a: It's mackerel from the Mae Klong bay, steamed and arranged in woven baskets until the neck has to be bent to fit — the meat is firm and rich. You can buy it to take home at shops in the Mae Klong market, such as Da Mae Klong Mackerel, which steams its own every day. Tell the shop you've got a long trip so they pack it well.

faq.q: Can I eat my way around Samut Songkhram in a single day?
faq.a: Yes, if you plan the order well. In the morning eat mackerel and walk the Maeklong Railway Market in town; at midday head down to Don Hoi Lot for razor clams and seafood; in the afternoon stop at a canalside cafe in Amphawa; then finish with the food at the Amphawa floating market in the evening.
